chunks: And from it, and pointing to it at that time, is the description of the Turks

I can see a people whose faces are like shields covered with rough-scraped skins. They dress themselves in silken and woollen clothes and hold dear excellent horses. Their killing and bloodshed shall take place freely till the wounded shall walk over the dead and the number of runners-away shall be less than those taken prisoner
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the Turks described in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) foretells the rise of the Turks (often interpreted as Mongols) with vivid imagery of their distinct appearance and martial prowess. The description of 'intense warfare' where the wounded walk over the dead reflects the historical chaos of the Mongol conquests, emphasizing the scale of destruction and the rarity of escape. This prophecy is significant in Shia scholarship as it links physical characteristics to historical destiny, offering a lens through which to view subsequent Islamic history.
